cmad.notes: SOHO is still operational (launched 1995-12-02, no StopDate) and participates in NASA's Heliophysics senior review of operating missions (referenced in the 2020 Senior Review, which assesses PDMP/CMAD status), so a CMAD is nominally expected. No consolidated SOHO mission-level CMAD was located via general web search, the SOHO/NASA-GSFC pages, or instrument-team sites. SOHO is a joint ESA/NASA mission with ESA-led operations, and calibration is documented per-instrument (e.g. LASCO C2/C3 photometric calibration papers) rather than in a single mission CMAD, which likely explains the absence. Recorded as an expected-but-not-located gap; proceeded with the remaining sources.

instrument_coverage.notes: Observatory records carry no downward instrument links, so instruments were found by reverse-lookup of the SPASE registry path https://spase-metadata.org/SMWG/Instrument/SOHO/ ; each hit's ObservatoryID was confirmed to equal spase://SMWG/Observatory/SOHO. The registry also contains a SOHO/Ephemeris record, which is trajectory/orbit data, not a science instrument, and is excluded from the roster. External ground truth: the Observatory Description states 'Twelve instruments comprised the payload,' matching the canonical SOHO payload (CDS, CELIAS, COSTEP, EIT, ERNE, GOLF, LASCO, MDI, SUMER, SWAN, UVCS, VIRGO). All 12 have SPASE Instrument records, so coverage is complete and no instrument team is invisible to registry-based discovery. The mission instruments landing page (soho.nascom.nasa.gov) could not be fetched (tool permission denied), but the sibling instrument records supplied each instrument's lead directly.

notes: Record type is Observatory, so the description paper is the mission/observatory OVERVIEW paper: Domingo, Fleck & Poland, 'The SOHO mission: An overview', Solar Physics 162 (1995), doi:10.1007/BF00733425. Paper selection is CONFIDENT: title contains 'mission'/'overview', it names the observatory, it appears at the start of operations (Dec 1995 = launch month), and it is the canonical, heavily-cited SOHO reference explicitly cited in the SPASE Description ('B. Fleck, V. Domingo, and A. I. Poland, eds., Solar Physics, V. 162, 1995'). SciX/Springer agree on the author list.

Overview-paper alphabetization check: only 3 authors (Domingo, Fleck, Poland), below the 5-name threshold, so treated as NOT alphabetized — author order signals contribution. All three are positions 1-3, hence Strong-tier.

Bernhard Fleck is corroborated at two levels: overview co-author (Strong) AND Observatory-record ProjectScientist (Medium). Vicente Domingo (first Project Scientist) and Arthur I. Poland (a later Project Scientist) are the other overview authors; both have SMWG Person records (Poland's is Arthur.I.Poland; the bare 'Arthur.Poland' slug returns 404).

The 12 instrument PIs are Medium via the qualifying PrincipalInvestigator role in their sibling SOHO Instrument records; per the skill, for an Observatory record all instrument leads are legitimate candidates. Every one has an existing SMWG Person record.

SPASE instrument records reflect CURRENT PIs for several instruments, which differ from the original description-paper-era PIs: CELIAS (Wimmer-Schweingruber now; originally D. Hovestadt / P. Bochsler), COSTEP (Heber now; originally H. Kunow), ERNE (Vainio now; originally J. Torsti), LASCO (Howard now; originally G. Brueckner). These original/founding instrument PIs were NOT asserted as candidates in this run because no source naming them was fetched here; a downstream instrument-level pass should recover them from each instrument's own description paper (several instrument records link one, e.g. CELIAS doi:10.1007/BF00733436, COSTEP doi:10.1007/BF00733437, ERNE doi:10.1007/BF00733438).
UVCS lists two PrincipalInvestigators in SPASE (John L. Kohl and J. Leonard Culhane); both retained as Medium candidates.
CMAD expected but not located — see the cmad object. SOHO participates in NASA senior review but calibration is documented per-instrument rather than in a consolidated mission CMAD.

The Observatory record carries no explicit OperatingSpan element; operating_span.start was taken from the launch date in the Description (1995-12-02) and stop set to null because SOHO remains operational. Downstream era-matching should use these values.
The SOHO/Ephemeris registry entry is orbit/trajectory data, not a science instrument; excluded from the instrument roster and generates no candidates.
